area.title: Layout, navigation, sign-in and shared page chrome
area.scope: What every page shares: the GOV.UK header, service name, service navigation and its items, phase banner and feedback link, footer, page title pattern, section captions, back links, error summary and shared error messages, error pages, the prototype index and version cards, sign-in, organisation choice, sign-out and sessions across services, security headers, and the accessibility and security suites. Stops at the journey's step order and scope rules (journey-flow). Includes the high-risk plants frontend's shared layout, kit, save actions and shared copy, and its chrome, sign-in, accessibility and Welsh rulings.

sources.role: the owner's decisions: outranks every other source. Search boxes use the real frontend's accessible component with MDM's entries. JavaScript behaviour follows the toolbox rule with graceful degradation; JavaScript-only prototype behaviour, pop-ups included, waits on design in its own theme. Commodity catalogue and search wait on MDM; transporter management waits on requirements; the INS dashboard's summary information waits on its requirements. The overview, review, declaration and confirmation are set-owned, and shared parts change add-only. Where plants has the same page or behaviour, the same increment changes it. Each notification list is reframed in its own frontend. The report groups work as ready or blocked. Claims marked as the orchestrator's apply Sam's principles and are not his rulings; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates covers templates and the dashboard narrowing.

claims.statement: The ruling's DR1 paragraph has an elision marked [...]: what the omitted words said about the DR1 parity backlog is not recorded.
The ruling does not say what makes a difference 'truly exceptional', so when a question for people is warranted is left open.

The ruling limits DR1 use to clashes between 'the real frontend' and the prototype; it does not say which frontend that is, or whether DR1 judgements apply to differences in the INS frontend, the backends or other repos.
The ruling does not say which override wins when a DR1 judgement and a real constraint the prototype cannot express point different ways on the same difference.
The ruling does not say what a real service does where a real constraint overrides the prototype: whether it keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as the constraint allows.
The ruling does not say whether a feature or behaviour a real service has that Design Release 2.1 does not show at all counts as a difference to remove, or is left alone.
The ruling does not say what to do where the code two themes need to touch overlaps, so no boundary keeps their pull requests from conflicting.

sources.role: how the real services behave end to end today

claims.statement: An unauthenticated user who opens the animals notification dashboard (/live-animals) is redirected to the frontend's sign-in route, which carries the requested path as a redirect parameter.
claims.quote: GET 302 http://localhost:3000/live-animals -> /auth/sign-in?redirect=%2Flive-animals

claims.statement: The frontend's sign-in route redirects the browser to the Defra ID authorise endpoint (the stub on localhost:3007) for the b2c_1a_cui_cpdev_signupsigninsfi policy.
claims.quote: http://localhost:3007/dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/b2c_1a_cui_cpdev_signupsigninsfi/oauth2/v2.0/authorize?serviceId=trade-imports-animals-frontend&p=b2c_1a_cui_cpdev_signupsigninsfi&response_mode=query&client_id=test-client-id&response_type=code&redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A3000%2Fauth%2Fsign-in-oidc&state=[REDACTED]&scope=openid%20offline_access%20test-client-id
claims.note: The state value differs per run; redacted here as a per-session value.

claims.statement: The authorise request is an OpenID Connect authorisation-code request: response_type code, response_mode query, scope openid offline_access plus the client id, and redirect_uri pointing at the frontend's /auth/sign-in-oidc callback.
claims.quote: response_mode=query&client_id=test-client-id&response_type=code&redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A3000%2Fauth%2Fsign-in-oidc

claims.statement: The authorise request names the calling service with a serviceId parameter of trade-imports-animals-frontend.
claims.quote: serviceId=trade-imports-animals-frontend

claims.statement: The Defra ID stub's authorise endpoint redirects to its own sign-in page at /dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp.
claims.quote: GET 302 ... /oauth2/v2.0/authorize?... -> /dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp

claims.statement: Opening the notification dashboard while signed out lands the user on the sign-in page, whose main heading is 'Sign in using Government Gateway'.
claims.quote: Sign in using Government Gateway

claims.statement: The sign-in page's browser title is 'Trade Imports Defra ID stub - GOV.UK'.
claims.quote: Trade Imports Defra ID stub - GOV.UK

claims.statement: The sign-in page's service navigation names the service 'Trade Imports Defra ID stub', and that service-name section is rendered twice, one under the other.
claims.ref: trace be93a action call@263 header section.govuk-service-navigation (two copies)
claims.quote: Trade Imports Defra ID stub
claims.note: The duplicate service navigation section is a rendering defect in the stub, not in the animals frontend.

claims.statement: The sign-in page carries a phase banner tagged 'Basic' with no banner text.
claims.quote: Basic

claims.statement: The sign-in page asks for a Government Gateway user ID in a text input (name crn).
claims.ref: trace be93a action call@263 label[for=crn], input#crn
claims.quote: Government Gateway user ID

claims.statement: The user ID field has the hint 'This could be up to 12 characters.'
claims.quote: This could be up to 12 characters.
claims.note: The hint says up to 12 characters while the error message asks for a 10-digit customer reference number (CRN); recorded, not reconciled.

claims.statement: The sign-in page asks for a password in a password-type input (name password).
claims.ref: trace be93a action call@263 label[for=password], input#password type=password
claims.quote: Password

claims.statement: The sign-in form submits with a button labelled 'Sign in'.
claims.quote: Sign in

claims.statement: The sign-in form posts the user ID and password as form-encoded fields crn and password to the stub's /dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp.
claims.quote: <FORM method="POST" action="/dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp"> ... crn=2100010101&password=[REDACTED]

claims.statement: Below the form, the sign-in page shows a link 'I have forgotten my password'; its href is '#', so it goes nowhere.
claims.ref: trace be93a action call@263 main p.govuk-body a.govuk-link
claims.quote: I have forgotten my password

claims.statement: The sign-in page has a Details component with the summary 'Help signing in'.
claims.ref: trace be93a action call@263 details.govuk-details summary
claims.quote: Help signing in

claims.statement: The 'Help signing in' details tell the user to contact the Rural Payments Agency if they have forgotten, lost or cannot get recognised their CRN.
claims.quote: Contact the Rural Payments Agency by email or phone if: you have forgotten your CRN / you have lost your CRN / your CRN is not recognised

claims.statement: The 'Help signing in' details give an email address, a telephone number and service opening times for the Rural Payments Agency.
claims.quote: Email: testing@farming.gov.uk / Telephone: 0300 000 0000 / Service opening times: 09:00 AM to 05:00 PM
claims.note: These are stub placeholder contact details.

claims.statement: The 'Help signing in' details link to GOV.UK call charges, opening in a new tab.
claims.quote: Find out about call charges (opens in new tab)

claims.statement: The 'Help signing in' details tell a user without an account to register with the Rural Payments service, linking to www.ruralpayments.service.gov.uk.
claims.quote: Register with the Rural Payments service if you do not have an account.

claims.statement: The sign-in page uses only GOV.UK Frontend components (Input, Button, Details, Service navigation, Phase banner, Error summary) plus the app-header and app-main-wrapper hooks.
claims.ref: trace be93a action call@263 class list of main and header
claims.quote: govuk-input govuk-input--width-20 ... govuk-button ... govuk-details ... govuk-main-wrapper app-main-wrapper

claims.statement: Signing in with a user ID that is not a valid customer reference number keeps the user on the sign-in page, and the stub answers the post with HTTP 400.
claims.quote: POST 400 http://localhost:3007/dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp crn=invalid&password=[REDACTED]

claims.statement: After a bad user ID, the sign-in page shows an error summary titled 'There is a problem' with the message 'Enter a valid 10-digit customer reference number (CRN) and password'.
claims.quote: There is a problem ... Error: Enter a valid 10-digit customer reference number (CRN) and password

claims.statement: Signing in with a valid user ID but a wrong password also keeps the user on the sign-in page with HTTP 400.
claims.quote: POST 400 http://localhost:3007/dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp crn=2100010101&password=[REDACTED]

claims.statement: After a wrong password, the sign-in page shows the same error summary and message as for a bad user ID, so the user is not told which of the two was wrong.
claims.quote: There is a problem ... Error: Enter a valid 10-digit customer reference number (CRN) and password

claims.statement: After a failed sign-in, the user ID field keeps the value entered and the password field is empty.
claims.ref: trace 8c7b9 action call@303 input#crn, input#password; trace 57464 action call@237
claims.quote: <INPUT ... id="crn" name="crn" type="text" value="invalid" ...> <INPUT ... id="password" name="password" type="password">

claims.statement: The sign-in error summary departs from the GOV.UK Error summary pattern: the message is a span inside the list rather than a list item linking to the field, and neither input is marked with a field-level error message or error class.
claims.quote: Error: Enter a valid 10-digit customer reference number (CRN) and password
claims.note: The standard component would replace this with an li containing an anchor to #crn, plus govuk-form-group--error and an inline error message on the field. This is the stub's page, not the animals frontend's.

claims.statement: A correct user ID and password make the stub redirect to its /organisations step, which immediately redirects back to the frontend's /auth/sign-in-oidc callback with an authorisation code and the original state; no organisation choice is shown.
claims.quote: POST 302 .../oauth2/authresp -> /organisations; GET 302 http://localhost:3007/organisations -> http://localhost:3000/auth/sign-in-oidc?code=[REDACTED]&state=[REDACTED]

claims.statement: The frontend's /auth/sign-in-oidc callback redirects the signed-in user to the path held in the original redirect parameter (here the dashboard /live-animals).
claims.quote: GET 302 http://localhost:3000/auth/sign-in-oidc?code=[REDACTED]&state=[REDACTED] -> /live-animals

claims.statement: Signing in from the dashboard lands the user on the notification dashboard at /live-animals, whose main heading is 'Import notification service'.
claims.quote: Import notification service

claims.statement: On sign-in the frontend sets a session cookie that lasts 4 hours (Max-Age 14400), HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax.
claims.quote: session=[REDACTED]; Max-Age=14400; Expires=Wed, 07 Oct 2026 21:40:15 GMT; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/

claims.statement: On sign-in the frontend also sets sid and crumb cookies, both HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict, and clears the temporary bell-defra-id cookie.
claims.quote: bell-defra-id=[REDACTED]; Max-Age=0; ... crumb=[REDACTED]; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/ ... sid=[REDACTED]; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/
claims.note: None of the cookies carries the Secure flag on the local http stack.

claims.statement: The dashboard's browser title repeats the service name: 'Import notification service - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
claims.quote: Import notification service - Import notification service - GOV.UK

claims.statement: Once signed in, the service navigation names the service 'Import notification service', linking to /live-animals.
claims.quote: Import notification service

claims.statement: Once signed in, the service navigation has four items in order: Dashboard, Address book, Manage account, Log out.
claims.quote: Dashboard / Address book / Manage account / Log out

claims.statement: On the dashboard the Dashboard navigation item is marked active (aria-current) and links to /live-animals.
claims.quote: Dashboard

claims.statement: The Address book navigation item links out to the separate address book service on another origin (localhost:3002/address-book).
claims.quote: Address book

claims.statement: The Manage account navigation item has href '#', so it goes nowhere yet.
claims.quote: Manage account

claims.statement: The sign-out control is a service navigation link labelled 'Log out' that points at /auth/sign-out.
claims.quote: Log out

claims.statement: The signed-in header shows no signed-in identity: no email address, name or 'signed in as' strip appears in the header or navigation.
claims.ref: trace 0b934 action call@259 header; trace 27de2 action call@262 (auth.spec.ts:57)
claims.quote: expect(getByText('test.user11@defra.gov.uk')).toHaveCount(0)
claims.note: In trace 27de2 the count-0 assertion finished (17555.6 ms) about 2 ms before the dashboard document finished loading (17557.9 ms), and its last DOM snapshot is still the stub sign-in page, so that trace alone does not prove the absence. The absence is confirmed from the dashboard header rendered in trace 0b934 call@259, which carries no user identity.

claims.statement: Clicking Log out calls /auth/sign-out, which redirects to the Defra ID end-session URL for the same policy with a post_logout_redirect_uri pointing back at the frontend's /auth/sign-out-oidc.
claims.quote: GET 302 http://localhost:3000/auth/sign-out -> http://localhost:3007/idphub/b2c/b2c_1a_cui_cpdev_signupsigninsfi/signout?post_logout_redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A3000%2Fauth%2Fsign-out-oidc

claims.statement: Signing out clears the frontend's sid cookie.
claims.quote: sid=[REDACTED]; Max-Age=0; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/
claims.note: Only sid is cleared in this response; the session cookie set at sign-in is not cleared here.

claims.statement: After Log out the user lands on the Defra ID stub's page with the heading 'You have signed out'.
claims.quote: You have signed out

claims.statement: The signed-out page tells the user they can return to GOV.UK (link opens in a new tab) or close the browser window.
claims.ref: trace ca937 action call@239 (stub signout page) main p.govuk-body
claims.quote: You can return to GOV.UK or close your browser window.

claims.statement: The signed-out page stays on the stub: the browser is not sent on to the frontend's /auth/sign-out-oidc, and the page offers no link back into the import notification service.
claims.ref: trace ca937 request log (last request GET /idphub/b2c/b2c_1a_cui_cpdev_signupsigninsfi/signout, status 200)
claims.quote: GET 200 http://localhost:3007/idphub/b2c/b2c_1a_cui_cpdev_signupsigninsfi/signout?post_logout_redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A3000%2Fauth%2Fsign-out-oidc

claims.statement: After signing out, reopening the notification dashboard sends the user back through sign-in to the 'Sign in using Government Gateway' page.
claims.ref: trace 03083 action call@345, call@349; request GET /live-animals (second) (auth.spec.ts:62)
claims.quote: GET 302 http://localhost:3000/live-animals -> /auth/sign-in?redirect=%2Flive-animals

claims.statement: Once signed in, opening the service root / redirects to the default set's dashboard, /live-animals, which shows the 'Import notification service' heading.
claims.ref: trace 71d40 action call@250, call@254; request GET / (auth.spec.ts:40)
claims.quote: GET 302 http://localhost:3000/ -> /live-animals
claims.note: The spec comment says no set is served at the root any more, so / is a server-wide redirect to the default set.

claims.statement: A signed-out user who opens a page further in the journey (/live-animals/notifications/<reference>/origin) is redirected to sign-in, with that full path kept in the redirect parameter.
claims.ref: trace 68f5b action call@295, call@299; request GET /live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-TBYAW8/origin (auth.spec.ts:87)
claims.quote: GET 302 http://localhost:3000/live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-TBYAW8/origin -> /auth/sign-in?redirect=%2Flive-animals%2Fnotifications%2FGBN-AG-26-TBYAW8%2Forigin

claims.statement: Signing in from a deep journey link returns the user to that journey page, 'Origin of the import', rather than to the dashboard.
claims.ref: trace d79c5 action call@301, call@303; request GET /auth/sign-in-oidc (second) (auth.spec.ts:92)
claims.quote: GET 302 http://localhost:3000/auth/sign-in-oidc?code=[REDACTED]&state=[REDACTED] -> /live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-BAZX13/origin

claims.statement: A draft's saved answers survive signing out and back in: on returning to the origin page after a fresh sign-in, France is still selected and the region-of-origin-code answer is still No.
claims.ref: trace d79c5 action call@301 select#countryOfOrigin-select, input#regionOfOriginCodeRequirement-2
claims.quote: <OPTION value="FR" selected="">France</OPTION> ... <INPUT ... id="regionOfOriginCodeRequirement-2" name="regionOfOriginCodeRequirement" type="radio" value="no" checked="">

claims.statement: The unauthenticated deep-link tests start from no session at all: the test keeps only cookies whose names start 'liveAnimals', and the browser held none (its cookies were trade-imports-defra-id-stub-session, crumb, sid and session), so every cookie was cleared before the deep link.
claims.ref: trace 68f5b action call@289 (cookies result), call@293 (addCookies with an empty list); trace d79c5 action call@283, call@287
claims.quote: const journeyCookies = (await pages.page.context().cookies()).filter(({ name }) => name.startsWith('liveAnimals'));
claims.note: Inferred from the cookie names the trace recorded and the empty addCookies call: the journey state is held server-side against the notification reference, not in a liveAnimals cookie.

claims.statement: The animals frontend sends a Content-Security-Policy header on the dashboard document response.
claims.quote: Content-Security-Policy: base-uri 'self';connect-src 'self' wss data:;default-src 'self';font-src 'self' data:;form-action 'self' http://localhost:3002;frame-ancestors 'none';frame-src 'self' data:;img-src 'self' data:;manifest-src 'self';media-src 'self';object-src 'none';script-src 'self' 'sha256-GUQ5ad8JK5KmEWmROf3LZd9ge94daqNvd8xy9YS1iDw=';style-src 'self';worker-src 'self'

claims.statement: The CSP restricts scripts to the frontend's own origin plus one inline script allowed by its SHA-256 hash.
claims.quote: script-src 'self' 'sha256-GUQ5ad8JK5KmEWmROf3LZd9ge94daqNvd8xy9YS1iDw='

claims.statement: The CSP lets forms post to the frontend itself and to the address book service's origin (localhost:3002).
claims.quote: form-action 'self' http://localhost:3002

claims.statement: The CSP forbids framing the frontend and forbids plugins and object embeds.
claims.quote: frame-ancestors 'none'; ... object-src 'none'

claims.statement: The CSP limits styles, fonts, images, media, manifests and workers to the frontend's own origin, with data: URIs also allowed for fonts, images, frames and connections.
claims.quote: connect-src 'self' wss data:;default-src 'self';font-src 'self' data:;frame-src 'self' data:;img-src 'self' data:;manifest-src 'self';media-src 'self';style-src 'self';worker-src 'self'

claims.statement: The CSP header is also present on the frontend's redirect responses (/live-animals 302 and /auth/sign-in 302) and on the /auth/sign-in-oidc callback, not only on rendered pages.
claims.quote: Content-Security-Policy

claims.statement: The dashboard response also sends Strict-Transport-Security for one year including subdomains.
claims.quote: strict-transport-security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains

claims.statement: The dashboard response sends X-Frame-Options DENY, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, X-Download-Options noopen and X-XSS-Protection '1; mode=block'.
claims.quote: x-frame-options: DENY; x-content-type-options: nosniff; x-download-options: noopen; x-xss-protection: 1; mode=block

claims.statement: The dashboard response is sent with Cache-Control no-cache.
claims.quote: cache-control: no-cache

claims.statement: The corpus never submits the sign-in form with an empty user ID or an empty password, so the message for missing credentials is not recorded.
claims.ref: auth.spec.ts (only 'invalid' user id and 'invalid' password cases); traces 8c7b9, 57464

claims.statement: No trace exercises session expiry: what a user sees when the 4-hour session cookie lapses, or whether a timeout warning is shown, is not recorded.
No trace follows the post-logout callback /auth/sign-out-oidc, so what the frontend does there (clearing the remaining session cookie, where it redirects) is not recorded.
The stub's /organisations step redirects straight back without showing a page, so the corpus never shows an organisation or business choice for a user linked to more than one organisation.
The service root / is only opened while signed in; whether an unauthenticated visit to / redirects to the default set first or straight to sign-in is not recorded.
The CSP and security headers are only recorded for the animals frontend; the Defra ID stub's sign-in and signed-out pages were not checked for them by any test.

claims.statement: INS sign-in hands off to Defra ID with an OIDC authorization-code request naming serviceId trade-imports-ins-frontend, the b2c_1a_cui_cpdev_signupsigninsfi policy, scope openid offline_access, and redirect_uri /auth/sign-in-oidc on the INS frontend.
claims.quote: oauth2/v2.0/authorize?serviceId=trade-imports-ins-frontend&p=b2c_1a_cui_cpdev_signupsigninsfi&response_mode=query&client_id=test-client-id&response_type=code&redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A3002%2Fauth%2Fsign-in-oidc

claims.statement: A signed-out user opening a page past the address book landing page lands on the Defra ID sign-in page, headed Sign in using Government Gateway, at .../oauth2/authresp.

claims.statement: Signing in to the animals frontend first means INS and then plants sign the user in without the credentials being asked for again: the Defra ID stub answers their authorize request straight away.
claims.ref: trace 3157d requests GET /dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp (INS and plants legs)
claims.quote: GET 302 http://localhost:3007/dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp -> http://localhost:3007/organisations

claims.statement: Each frontend signs in with its own serviceId and its own /auth/sign-in-oidc callback: trade-imports-animals-frontend on port 3000, trade-imports-ins-frontend on 3002, trade-imports-plants-frontend on 3003.
claims.quote: serviceId=trade-imports-animals-frontend ... serviceId=trade-imports-ins-frontend ... serviceId=trade-imports-plants-frontend

claims.statement: Having signed in to animals, INS and plants in one browser, revisiting each dashboard opens it directly (200) with no further sign-in: all three sessions are kept.
claims.quote: GET 200 http://localhost:3000/live-animals / GET 200 http://localhost:3002/ / GET 200 http://localhost:3003/high-risk-plants

claims.statement: Each service keeps its session in its own cookie on the shared host, so the three do not overwrite each other: sid (animals), ins-sid and ins-session (INS), plants-sid (plants), plus the identity stub's trade-imports-defra-id-stub-session; all are HttpOnly, the -sid cookies SameSite Strict and the session cookies SameSite Lax.
claims.quote: crumb, sid, ins-sid, ins-session, trade-imports-defra-id-stub-session, plants-sid, session
claims.note: Which service owns the plain 'session' cookie is not shown.

claims.statement: After a failed sign-in the stub's browser title stays 'Trade Imports Defra ID stub - GOV.UK' with no 'Error: ' prefix, unlike the animals frontend's own error pages.
claims.ref: trace 8c7b9 action call@303 <title>; trace 57464 action call@237
claims.quote: Trade Imports Defra ID stub - GOV.UK
claims.note: This is the stub's page, not the animals frontend's.

claims.statement: The sign-in error summary is placed inside the form, below the H1, rather than at the top of the main content above the heading.
claims.quote: Sign in using Government Gateway
claims.note: GOV.UK guidance puts the error summary at the top of the main container, before the h1. This is the stub's page.

claims.statement: The frontend's /auth/sign-in route can itself set the bell-defra-id cookie and the 4-hour session cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax) on its redirect to Defra ID, before the user has signed in.
claims.quote: bell-defra-id=[REDACTED]; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/ || session=[REDACTED]; Max-Age=14400; Expires=Wed, 07 Oct 2026 21:40:15 GMT; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/
claims.note: In trace 0b934 the same session cookie is recorded on /auth/sign-in-oidc instead and /auth/sign-in records no Set-Cookie, so the trace shows where cookies land inconsistently between runs.

claims.statement: The dashboard page carries the CSRF token in a csrf-token meta tag whose value equals the crumb cookie, and the frontend's form posts send it as a crumb field.
claims.ref: trace 0b934 action call@257 <head> meta[name=csrf-token]; request GET /auth/sign-in-oidc Set-Cookie crumb; trace d79c5 request POST /live-animals/notifications
claims.quote: <META name="csrf-token" content="GpGSRc9hok7ZX7i16rIoO6rNchFk5BQ5F6nr-RpPdhE"> ... crumb=GpGSRc9hok7ZX7i16rIoO6rNchFk5BQ5F6nr-RpPdhE; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/

claims.statement: The signed-out page's 'return to GOV.UK' link opens in a new tab (target=_blank) without saying so in its text, unlike the sign-in page's '(opens in new tab)' call-charges link.
claims.ref: trace ca937 action call@239 main p.govuk-body a
claims.quote: You can return to GOV.UK or close your browser window.
claims.note: This is the stub's page.

claims.statement: Signing in again after sign-out, or after the session is lost, always asks for the user ID and password again: the stub never signs the user straight back in.
claims.ref: trace 03083 requests after call@345 (GET 200 /dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp); trace d79c5 action call@291 (fill user ID again)
claims.quote: GET 302 http://localhost:3007/dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/b2c_1a_cui_cpdev_signupsigninsfi/oauth2/v2.0/authorize?... -> /dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp; GET 200 http://localhost:3007/dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp
claims.note: Inferred from the stub rendering its sign-in form every time the authorise endpoint is hit, even with its own stub-session cookie still held (03083), so the stub does not model single sign-on. Real Defra ID may behave differently.

claims.statement: The frontend's CSP also restricts the document base URL and the default source to its own origin.
claims.quote: base-uri 'self';connect-src 'self' wss data:;default-src 'self'

claims.statement: The CSP's connect-src lists 'wss' without a colon, which CSP reads as a host named wss rather than the secure-WebSocket scheme, so it probably does not allow what it was meant to.
claims.quote: connect-src 'self' wss data:
claims.note: Inferred from CSP source-expression grammar: a scheme source needs a trailing colon (wss:), as data: has here.

claims.statement: The Defra ID stub sends its own, stricter CSP on its sign-in page (default-src 'none', per-response nonces for scripts and styles, frame-ancestors 'self'), with form-action 'self' * so its form can post anywhere.
claims.quote: base-uri 'self';connect-src 'self';default-src 'none';font-src 'self';form-action 'self' *;frame-ancestors 'self';img-src 'self';manifest-src 'self';script-src 'self' 'sha256-GUQ5ad8JK5KmEWmROf3LZd9ge94daqNvd8xy9YS1iDw=' 'nonce-548e0673686120d75c269d913ee55586';style-src 'self' 'nonce-b23b4b8c61068f530ed714eb547ec7ea';worker-src 'self'
claims.note: No test asserts these (claim 067 holds as a gap about test coverage), but the network log records them.

claims.statement: The animals frontend sends no Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy or Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy header on the dashboard, while the Defra ID stub sends all four on its sign-in page.
claims.ref: trace 6b20c request GET /live-animals response headers; trace be93a request GET /dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp response headers
claims.quote: Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp; Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin; Permissions-Policy: camera=(), geolocation=(), magnetometer=(), microphone=(), payment=(), usb=(); Referrer-Policy: same-origin; X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow
claims.note: The quote is the stub's headers; the frontend's absence is read from the full header list of 6b20c's /live-animals response (Connection, Content-Security-Policy, Date, Keep-Alive, Transfer-Encoding, cache-control, content-encoding, content-type, set-cookie, strict-transport-security, vary and the four x- headers only).

claims.statement: The animals and plants frontends share one CSRF cookie: both use a cookie named crumb on localhost, and every form on the animals dashboard and the plants dashboard carries the same crumb value, so one service's crumb is accepted by the other's forms.
claims.ref: trace 3157d call@23 and call@41 snapshots (hidden crumb inputs); call@69 cookies result
claims.quote: name="crumb" value="[REDACTED]" (one identical value in the animals /live-animals and plants /high-risk-plants forms)
claims.note: Inferred from identical crumb values in both frontends' forms and a single crumb cookie; whether a cross-service POST would actually be accepted is not exercised.
